newsitem.title: UK: NZ SPORT-Newcastle signs Inga for cool NZ$2.35 mln.
newsitem.headline: NZ SPORT-Newcastle signs Inga for cool NZ$2.35 mln.

text.p: LONDON, Feb 19 - Wealthy northern England club Newcastle has completed Va'aiga Tuigamala's full-time return to rugby union, signing him from rugby league giants Wigan on a contract worth over Stg1 million ($NZ2.35 million), NZPA reported on Thursday (NZT).

The deal had been an open secret for some weeks, but Newcastle, whose chairman and paymaster Sir John Hall flew in especially from Spain for the unveiling, caused a minor surprise when they announced a five-year contract, rather than the three years expected.
Tuigamala, the former All Black winger, becomes the first million pound player in either code and is the latest high-profile league player to turn his back on the 13-man game.
Newcastle, the second division club who now boast 14 internationals including Western Samoa captain Pat Lam, unveiled Tuigamala today after weeks of speculation.
In the deal, Newcastle paid a Stg500,000 transfer fee as well as repaying the Super League "loyalty" payments, and the balance of Tuigamala's three-year deal at Wigan.
Tuigamala, 27, made a temporary return to union ranks on loan to Wasps last year, and even rekindled his international career with Western Samoa, helping them to a 40-25 win over Ireland in Dublin.
The announcement today will be welcomed by Western Samoa rugby supporters.

Though Tuigamala played 19 tests for New Zealand before turning to league, he is now a declared Western Samoa player and the way is now clear for him to appear for his country of birth in the 1999 World Cup in Britain.
He toured to Canada, Wales and Ireland with the All Blacks in 1989, and played in the 1991 World Cup in Britain.

But there was a flaw to Tuigamala, who struggled with a weight problem and gained a reputation as a lazy trainer. By the time he turned to league in 1993, he had lost his place on the Auckland team to Waisake Sotutu and was facing an uncertain future.

Tuigamala took his weight problem with him to Wigan, where he quickly earned the nickname "Puffing Billy", but the pressures of professionalism and Wigan's fitness regime, under coach Graeme West, soon honed him down to around 16 stone.
Tuigamala said: "The move to Newcastle has presented me with an opportunity that I just couldn't turn down -- an opportunity that enables me to return to the game I was brought up on.
"I've had three marvellous years at Central Park and have never once regretted my decision to leave the All Blacks and play professional rugby league at Wigan."

Tuigamala, born in Western Samoa on September 4 1969, first came to prominence in New Zealand in 1988 and 1989 with a string of powerhouse displays for Auckland and the New Zealand Colts, when he played alongside fellow union convert Craig Innes.
He won the Wigan fans over with a string of bruising performances on the field, and an engaging personality off it.
Rugby union's new-found professionalism was a new attraction in 1996, with Tuigamala agreeing to a temporary deal with London club Wasps, who reportedly paid him Stg5000 a match.
His impact with Wasps and Western Samoa inevitably brought on a high-priced auction which Newcastle won.
Tuigamala said: "I thought long and hard about the deal and I accepted five years because I have so much to give and so much to achieve. I believe my best rugby will develop in that time.
"I have always been an ambitious person, setting my goals and setting my own standards, and I see Newcastle as a further opportunity to achieve some of those goals.
"I see the club going places and I feel honoured and privileged to be part of the set up."
Tuigamala had always maintained, even when he was a league player, that he would end his career in the 15-man code.
Newcastle's director of rugby, Rob Andrew, said the club will be using Tuigamala's profile and personality to promote the game in England's north-east.
He said he had always been a fan of Tuigamala, "particularly after he ran all over me when I was playing for the British Lions in the second test in 1993."
